rv.q: While this is at times a noisily unsubtle show, its defining quality is a warm and joyful energy.
Yet so many bizarrely tone-deaf choices have been made on the part of the creative team.
But Luke Sheppard’s production, although powered by plenty of candy-coloured pizzazz, can’t capture the subversive spirit that made Mole so delectable on the page.
The energetic cast, under Luke Sheppard’s zippy direction, is a joy to watch.

It is a very loud, rather tiring night; I found I was enjoying episodes such as the high-energy school disco and Adrian's alternative nativity play which sends Mary to the family planning clinic and makes the inn keeper an evil capitalist, while simultaneously wishing them just a little less broad and energetic.

cn.t: This musical adaptation of Sue Townsend's beloved novel delivers an entertaining romp through teenage awkwardness, reveling in the lovelorn disappointments and comedic dramas of the famously spotty adolescent diarist.
